bugs.text: Divers that leave the bottom come back from below the screen (y0=H+26) and fly up to their slot through the player's row, where they can still ram the player; spec says re-enter from the top.
Dual fighter: a hit on either half calls killPlayer() after clearing dual, so the whole ship and a life are lost instead of only that half.
Challenging-stage enemies fire: scheduleFiring has no challenging check and treats 'entering' fly-through enemies as shooters.
Capture has no pull-up: the ship explodes with the death sound and a red ship pops up above the Boss.
If the beam catches the side half of a dual fighter, a reserve life is also deducted although the second ship was never counted as a life.
Captured fighter fires only while its Boss sits in formation, not when the Boss dives.
Formation sways and breathes at the same time throughout; no distinct sway-then-breathe phases.
Entering/returning enemies end at a static slot position and snap to the moving slotPos (visible jump).
Enemies in the 'returning' state (and the Boss in 'postBeam'/'returning' for rescue) count as formation: formation points and the captive is destroyed instead of freed.
A freed ship docks even while the player is dead/respawning, then respawnPlayer clears dual, so the rescued ship is silently lost.
sHit is never used; the stage jingle plays only at game start, not before each stage.
Title screen shows 'CREDIT' with the leftover lives count (CREDIT 0 after a game).

summary: A compact, cleanly sectioned single-file clone with a correct fixed-timestep loop, integer-scaled 224x288 playfield, good HUD, title, stage intro, game-over hit stats and localStorage high score; it ran 90 s of bot play with no errors and cycled game over back to title. Formation layout, scoring (including escort bonuses and challenge-stage wave/perfect bonuses), two-hit purple Boss, curved group entries, stage-scaled dives and a convincing widening tractor beam are all present. Fidelity drops in the signature details: capture blows up the ship instead of pulling it up, a hit on the dual fighter kills both halves, the captive fires from formation rather than on dives, challenge-stage enemies still shoot, and divers come back up from the bottom of the screen instead of the top. Graphics are small and simple but readable; overall it feels like Galaga with several rule shortcuts.
